name: Ontario Hall
summary: The six-storey wings use taupe brick, red-brown projecting piers, and narrower buff strips, with light blue glass marking the ends. A lower common block and a setback upper floor complete the arrival court.

evidence.note: The east wing terminates in a tall glass strip. Deep masonry piers separate paired vertical stacks of windows.
The north arrival court has a fully glazed corner and tall glazing between masonry piers.
Silver vertical frames and blue-grey spandrels sit beside dark textured stone and copper-coloured rectangular panels. A stone retaining wall follows the foreground.
The courtyard photograph confirms paired tall openings, orange panel bands, and narrow projecting dark stone piers.
The common block has a two-storey glazed entrance behind wide steps and handrails.
Western Residence identifies six occupied levels.
Three narrow wings project south around open courts. The cross-wing has a lower roof between the wings, larger roof volumes, and scattered metal plant.
Inventory P50 / P90 / maximum: 20.06 / 22.03 / 25.28 m above local ground.

notes: The copper-coloured panels occur on selected bays and storeys. Vertical strips alternate glazing and opaque spandrel panels. The depth of the central common block and window counts on the back of each wing are estimates.
